basics.name: Kundan Nandy
basics.title: Java Backend Engineer · Spring Boot & Microservices @ Capgemini
basics.summary: I build backend systems that handle real traffic — scalable REST APIs, microservices architectures, and Spring Boot applications that teams can actually maintain and extend. Currently at Capgemini (2.4 years), I work on Java/Spring Boot–based services used in enterprise-scale workflows. My day-to-day spans end-to-end feature development, API design, performance optimization, and cross-team delivery.

bullets: Designed and developed RESTful microservices using Java 17 and Spring Boot, contributing to an enterprise-scale backend platform; services integrated with 7 downstream systems and handled 30K daily requests.
Implemented data persistence layers using Spring Data JPA and Hibernate; optimized SQL queries and reduced average API response time by 30% through indexing and query restructuring.
Built and versioned REST APIs consumed by front-end and third-party teams; collaborated across 3+ squads to define contracts and ensure backward compatibility.
Accelerated local development by reducing boilerplate code using Lombok, and streamlined API testing workflows using Postman collections shared across the team.
Participated in code reviews for 10+ PRs per sprint, enforcing SOLID principles and catching bugs pre-production; contributed to reducing post-release defects in the service layer.
Delivered end-to-end features across full development lifecycle — from requirements breakdown to testing, deployment, and post-release monitoring.
Developed and maintained backend modules using Java, Spring Boot, and Maven, focusing on building scalable microservices and RESTful APIs, which improved application performance by 25%.
Designed and implemented JasperReports for automated PDF generation, reducing manual reporting effort by 40% and streamlining business workflows.
Collaborated using GitHub and Azure DevOps Repos for version control and CI/CD integration, while conducting thorough unit testing with JUnit and Mockito, increasing code reliability by 30%.

extra: Writing code that's readable 6 months later. Designing APIs that don't become maintenance nightmares. Shipping features that actually close business requirements.
